protocol_matrix.documented_transport: codex app-server: bidirectional stdio JSONL; JSON-RPC-shaped messages omit jsonrpc. Initialize then initialized.
protocol_matrix.request: item/commandExecution/requestApproval or item/fileChange/requestApproval; id plus threadId/turnId/itemId. Command/cwd/reason can be optional.
protocol_matrix.response: Echo server request id with a result decision payload; documented choices accept, acceptForSession, decline, cancel (commands also offer policy amendments). Observe availableDecisions where present.
protocol_matrix.cancel: turn/interrupt(threadId,turnId); empty success result is request acknowledgement; wait turn/completed status interrupted. serverRequest/resolved clears answered/withdrawn pending requests; item/completed provides final item status.
protocol_matrix.distinct_flows: networkApprovalContext requires a network-specific prompt. item/permissions/requestApproval grants only requested permission subsets. MCP elicitation and user questions are separate flows.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: Current documented v2 surface; installed CLI build and generated schema unknown. Exact decision-result member/schema must be bound to approved executable schema before implementing; no wire object guessed here.

protocol_matrix.documented_transport: codex exec is non-interactive. Ordinary progress is stderr; final answer stdout. --json supplies JSONL events such as thread.started, turn.completed and item.*.
protocol_matrix.request_response: Event observation is not the App Server bidirectional approval exchange. The inspected route supplies no --json and merges stderr with stdout.
protocol_matrix.cancel: Current spaCR requests direct-child termination/escalation; no provider turn acknowledgement is consumed and failed termination may leave worker/child pending.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: Current docs do not establish behavior of the extension-bundled CLI or reported macOS binary. Do not infer effective sandbox/approval policy from documentation defaults.

protocol_matrix.documented_transport: claude -p is print/headless mode; text/json/stream-json output and text/stream-json input are documented.
protocol_matrix.request_response: Current no-host print runs deny unresolved prompts; an SDK canUseTool host or --permission-prompt-tool MCP host can answer. JSON output alone supplies no GUI host. The MCP prompt tool has separate restrictions, including interaction-required tools since2.1.199.
protocol_matrix.cancel: Current docs: SIGTERM leaves the active turn without a result and a pending permission unanswered; SIGINT or SDK interrupt ends the turn first. SDK session close ends input/cancels the prompt. This is documentation, not measured installed behavior.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: --permission-prompts requires2.1.259+, older versions reject it. No flag change proposed; file-named2.1.282 and user macOS build do not attest these semantics. MCP response schema was not established here; no raw control_request format invented.
protocol_matrix.platform_qualification: On POSIX, the current Popen.terminate call sends SIGTERM and timeout escalation requests SIGKILL; on Windows, terminate invokes TerminateProcess and kill aliases it. Claude documented SIGTERM turn/prompt/Bash-child cleanup is current signal-specific vendor documentation, not installed-release, Windows or universal descendant acceptance. SDK interrupt/close are distinct protocol/lifecycle operations. Confirm any future adapter per supported OS/build; no such runtime acceptance is delivered here.

protocol_matrix.documented_transport: Claude Agent SDK streaming client, not the current text subprocess API.
protocol_matrix.request: can_use_tool(tool_name,input_data,context) / TS canUseTool; can pause for tool permission or AskUserQuestion. Separate question UI; callbacks occur only where policy resolves to a prompt.
protocol_matrix.response: Python PermissionResultAllow(updated_input=original_input) or PermissionResultDeny(message=reason,interrupt=False); a proposal should default to one action and no updated_permissions. Context tool_use_id identifies a call.
protocol_matrix.cancel: Python ClaudeSDKClient.interrupt works in streaming mode; drain receive_response through ResultMessage before another query. Current terminal_reason values include aborted_streaming/aborted_tools. Python context.signal is reserved; TS options.signal is AbortSignal. Pending callback cleanup must be implemented/verified explicitly.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: CLI plus SDK release/schema must both be pinned; no matching SDK distribution metadata found in inspected spaCR env. No dependency install or auth migration authorized.

protocol_matrix.documented_transport: -p or a non-TTY triggers headless mode. --output-format stream-json emits init,message,tool_use,tool_result,error,result.
protocol_matrix.request_response: A tool_use observation is not an ACP permission request and documents no selected-option reply channel. The current route supplies no output-format flag.
protocol_matrix.cancel: Current spaCR requests direct-child termination/escalation; no provider turn acknowledgement is consumed and failed termination may leave worker/child pending.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: No PATH executable identified; installed Gemini release and runtime behavior unknown.

protocol_matrix.documented_transport: Current Gemini docs use gemini --acp, JSON-RPC2.0 over stdio. ACP v1 initialize negotiates protocolVersion/capabilities; unsupported selected version closes rather than guesses compatibility.
protocol_matrix.request: session/request_permission has JSON-RPC id, sessionId, toolCall and options with optionId/name/kind.
protocol_matrix.response: Echo id; result.outcome is {outcome:selected,optionId:<exact offered ID>} or {outcome:cancelled}. Persistent choices are distinct from once-only options.
protocol_matrix.cancel: Send session/cancel notification; answer every pending permission cancelled. Accept remaining session/update notifications until original session/prompt returns stopReason cancelled. Local provisional cancellation is not that final proof.
protocol_matrix.version_scope: Gemini ACP guide uses conceptual method labels such as newSession; exact wire names here come from ACPv1. Verify executable flag and negotiated version; no installed support asserted.

current_source_findings.fact: Current argv are claude -p prompt, codex exec prompt, gemini -p prompt plus existing models. stdin=None inherits launch context; stdout PIPE and stderr STDOUT, no explicit cwd, inherited environment. Optional stdin_text writes once/closes. No GUI-owned response transport or chat PTY.
current_source_findings.consequence: Cannot answer approval by displaying a button without a supported response protocol. No claim inherited stdin is DEVNULL/unavailable everywhere.

current_source_findings.fact: Only connecting/streaming/string chunks/finished signals exist; streaming emitted before the lazy provider launches/receives data. No approval IDs, request state, decision callback or response API.
current_source_findings.consequence: Current status is not evidence of an actual pending approval or active tool. Plain assistant advice requesting a nonexistent button stays text.

current_source_findings.fact: Noise filter drops only exact Permission deny/allow/ask rule prefixes. It neither recognizes typed requests nor proves the reported approval text was filtered.
current_source_findings.consequence: Future protocol framing must precede display/noise handling; never infer grants from these advisory lines.

current_source_findings.fact: Cancel marks the tracked child as stopped-by-spaCR and requests terminate; it bounded-waits and requests kill only after a termination wait timeout. Signal/wait errors are swallowed. StreamWorker.cancel sets a local flag and calls the provider; it emits no finished signal. run reports Cancelled only after iteration or exception handling regains control. If the stdout read stays blocked and termination fails, completion may remain pending. _stream_process cleanup removes handles only when exit is confirmed; an uncertain child stays on the provider and in _LIVE_STREAMS for later shutdown retry.
current_source_findings.consequence: Cancel requested, a stopped marker and local worker state do not prove transport termination. Even a confirmed direct-child exit is not vendor turn/tool acknowledgement, descendant cessation or rollback. Do not show confirmed cancellation solely from the flag or a terminate request; preserve findable uncertain children and distinguish worker completion, child exit and provider terminal evidence.

current_source_findings.fact: SignInDialog owns a PTY login UI. Current login commands are claude auth login, codex login and gemini. Chat subprocesses use a separate text route.
current_source_findings.consequence: Successful login/sign-in is not tool permission or a chat approval-response implementation.

current_source_findings.fact: Natural nonzero child exit becomes ProviderFailed; natural successful text is accepted as an answer. Model/speed flags select models, not provider versions/capabilities.
current_source_findings.consequence: Provider-level denial may occur within otherwise successful text; exit0 is not evidence of tool completion or permission granted.

proposed_adapter_boundaries: Owner chooses explicit per-provider supported adapter/version matrix before coding; unknown versions get no tool-approval capability claim. Current text routes may explain unavailable approval safely, without granting anything.

Recognize genuine requests only at the top-level framed protocol/typed SDK callback of the selected adapter. Never promote prose, nested agent/tool text, stderr diagnostics, tool-use observations or JSON-looking conversation content into a permission event.

Bind each pending request to provider connection generation, conversation/session/thread, turn and call/request IDs. Preserve supplied action, cwd/path/network scope and exact offered options. Never grant based on a heuristic label or assistant assertion.

Only explicit per-request user approval may return a supported once-only choice; absent action details/options remain unavailable, not reconstructed. Reject stale, duplicate, mismatched or withdrawn replies. No timeout, close, login success, reconnect or generic prior yes yields approval.

Approval UI cannot weaken provider sandbox, managed denials, trust, hooks or account/tool policy. No bypass flags, auto-grant, inferred permission, policy amendment, persistent allow rule, mode switch or permission broadening is proposed.

Keep deny-one-action, cancel-turn, timeout, protocol failure and transport termination distinct. Owner must define bounded timeout; timeout sends supported deny/cancel or ends transport with cancellation-unconfirmed status, never an allow.

GUI remains responsive: deliver structured requests to GUI through queued signals, keep decisions/writes serialized off GUI, clean up pending prompts on provider withdrawal/cancel/error/shutdown. Unsupported callback cancellation must be tested rather than assumed.

Keep ordinary user questions, login/authentication, MCP elicitation and permission escalation separate. Do not advertise FS/terminal or other client capabilities until their host operations have explicit scope and owning contracts.
Keep stderr diagnostic handling separate from protocol stdout in a future structured transport; do not reparse existing merged text stream as an approval RPC.

Provider tool terminal state and whole-turn terminal state need separate receipts. Interrupted turn or exited child does not retroactively undo completed side effects. No work/account modification occurs in this review.

On POSIX, the current Popen.terminate call sends SIGTERM and timeout escalation requests SIGKILL; on Windows, terminate invokes TerminateProcess and kill aliases it. Claude documented SIGTERM turn/prompt/Bash-child cleanup is current signal-specific vendor documentation, not installed-release, Windows or universal descendant acceptance. SDK interrupt/close are distinct protocol/lifecycle operations. Confirm any future adapter per supported OS/build; no such runtime acceptance is delivered here.

future_acceptance_plan_not_run.expectation: Plain approval-required prose, permission-rule warning, stderr diagnostic, nested JSON-like assistant content and tool_use observation produce no approval dialog or decision write; a valid typed request does.

Once-only allow/deny returns exactly the selected offered decision to exact connection/request/call. Decline one action differs from cancel whole turn. No write on absent details, invalid option, duplicate, stale or foreign IDs.
Concurrent requests, out-of-order item completion, withdrawal/resolution, reconnect and provider change cannot leak approval into another conversation or resurrect a dismissed prompt.

Cancel during pending permission and during running tool uses provider-specific supported response/interrupt, drains terminal data and distinguishes acknowledgement from terminal proof. Late updates do not enter a subsequent turn.

Partial/malformed/oversized lines, no-newline output, unsupported method/schema, closed/broken stdin, nonzero exit, missing terminal event and deadline failure remain non-granting and keep GUI controls live.

Existing denied action remains denied despite GUI clicks; test no broadening flags/persistent updates. Login tests cannot satisfy permission tests. Avoid storing raw prompt/input/auth fields in public receipts.

Owner-approved installed release/build plus bound protocol schema, OS and effective restrictive policy; controlled harmless tool with approve/deny/cancel/timeout, no side effects before grant, actual terminal proof and native responsive GUI. Separate macOS1.5.1.4 reproduction from fixed-candidate tests. No provider sessions authorized now.
